A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyperGaussians with the same authors and core formulation. All 16 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original avatar reconstruction results, quantitative ablations, computational benchmarks, and appendix comparisons involving GaussianHeadAvatar and NDGS.

after.justification: v3 retains original monocular results and reports aggregate multi-view reconstruction results, NDGS comparisons, ablations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Gaussian conditioning, the inverse covariance trick and the FlashAvatar integration are retained. GaussianHeadAvatar integration already appears in v1 Appendix A.2.3; v3 Section 3.3 and Appendix C document its implementation more fully without establishing a changed procedure. The Bayesian treatment adds interpretation rather than a new training objective.

E1.justification: v3 lists five rather than four monocular source datasets, newly including NerFACE, but retains 19 subjects and identical aggregate scores. NeRSemble multi-view reconstruction already appears in v1 Appendix A.2.3. Without a corresponding v1 subject inventory, the PDFs do not establish whether represented data changed or dataset attribution was corrected.

E2.justification: v1 compares NDGS within FlashAvatar, while its GaussianHeadAvatar comparison contains only the baseline and HyperGaussians. v3 adds NDGS to the GaussianHeadAvatar comparison in Table 3 and Figure 10. The monocular comparator set remains unchanged; newly discussed feed-forward and diffusion methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The stated monocular resolution, frame split, metrics and 30k training iterations are unchanged. For GaussianHeadAvatar, v3 specifies 600k iterations and a detailed multi-view protocol, whereas v1 lacks corresponding settings and reports 9–9.5 hours instead of over two days. Whether the underlying protocol changed or was newly documented cannot be reliably determined.

E4.justification: v3 extends NDGS failure analysis to GaussianHeadAvatar, examining displaced glasses, weak reflections and disappearing wrinkles. Table 4 also extends the latent-dimension analysis with rendering FPS. The accuracy, MLP-size, convergence and uncertainty analyses largely already exist in v1, although their placement changes.

E5.justification: Both versions average the conditioning benchmark over 1000 runs after warm-up and retain the same covariance-based uncertainty measure and visualization. v3 adds no reported seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for reconstruction quality.

E6.justification: v3 adds aggregate multi-view results: Table 1 reports PSNR 24.10 for GaussianHeadAvatar and 24.38 for HyperGaussians, with equal reported SSIM; Table 3 adds NDGS at 24.22 PSNR. These are not directly comparable with v1 Figure 10's individual-example scores. v3 also adds multi-view qualitative results and FPS entries across latent dimensions. Monocular reconstruction and accuracy-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds the MAP equality in Equation 4, a conditional-support argument distinguishing HyperGaussians from NDGS, and explicit computational and parameter-complexity bounds. The Gaussian-conditioning, Cholesky and uncertainty derivations are substantially retained from v1.

C1.justification: The central claims of greater expressivity, efficient conditioning and easy integration remain. v3 adds probabilistic justification as an explicit contribution and broadens the abstract and conclusion to both pipelines and 29 subjects across six datasets. Multi-view applicability itself was already claimed and illustrated in v1's appendix.

C2.justification: v3 adds an implicit-prior regularization explanation, interprets uncertainty caused by unstable foreground masks, and suggests a memory-locality explanation for the 1D FPS anomaly. It removes v1's explicit caveats about inheriting the host method's limitations and unresolved scaling to thousands of dimensions. The existing local-context explanation is retained.

D1.justification: v3 substantially documents the previously brief GaussianHeadAvatar case study: attribute-specific latents, preprocessing, ten NeRSemble subject IDs, sequence selection, 16 cameras, 2048 × 2048 images and 600k iterations. It also states that an implementation is publicly released. Reported multi-view training time changes from 9–9.5 hours to over two days with 30 minutes of overhead, without explaining the cross-version difference.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning through 6DGS/7DGS and recent feed-forward and diffusion-based avatars. The enlarged related-work table distinguishes optimization, feed-forward and pseudo-ground-truth approaches and their resource requirements. v3 also claims a unified probabilistic interpretation of earlier high-dimensional Gaussian methods.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the introduction, related work and method exposition, divides the case studies and experiments into monocular and multi-view settings, and reorganizes the supplement into Appendices A–E. Model-scaling discussion moves into the main text, while uncertainty and latent-dimensionality discussion move into the supplement.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the teaser with GaussianHeadAvatar examples, expands multi-view comparison displays, adds aggregate comparison tables, and enlarges the related-work table with resource categories. It consolidates ablation displays and adds an FPS column. Conditioning, uncertainty and convergence figures are retained but relocated, producing substantial visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its second integration mainly through two illustrated multi-view examples with little implementation or evaluation detail. v3 supplies aggregate ten-subject results, an NDGS control and detailed integration and data protocols, substantially strengthening the assessability and reproducibility of the broader applicability claim. The unchanged monocular evidence is preserved. Dropped limitations and unexplained dataset-count and training-time differences remain weaknesses, but the gains in empirical support and documentation outweigh them.
